To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the progression of Gof p53 papilloma to carcinoma was marked with the acquisition of epithelia-to-mesenchyme transition and metastatic signature; (2) LOF p53 papillomata progressed to squamous cell carcinoma with a gene expression profile that was enriched in genes associated with proliferation and chromosomal stability.
we have identified Myc as a target of GOF mutant p53 and demonstrated that Myc amplification and Aurora A activation are critical events in GOF mutant p13 skin cancer progression.

the gain-of-function p53 mutation R172H, which is the most common p53 mutation found in human skin cancer, promotes genomic instability, Myc overexpression, and Aurora Kinase A deregulation, leading to the development of metastatic SCC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapies for the treatment of skin tumors.
the identification of novel targets in mutant p54 tumors, which may lead the development of novel therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of metastatic cancers.
the study of the role of mutant p53 proteins in the development of human cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GOF p53 mutations have a more prominent role in the progression of papillomas to invasive SCCs, while LOF p53 mutations are associated with genomic instability, which is a prominent feature of SCCs.
the GOF p53 mutation in the skin cancer model is a strong driver of the disease, which is associated with genomic instability and a high propensity to metastasize.
the p53 mutation in this model of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) has an effect on both genomic instability and the metastatic potential of the tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the gain of function of a mutant p53R72H protein in a model of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) progression is accompanied by genomic instability, which is associated with the preferential amplification and activation of Myc and Aurora Kinase A and the acquisition of a metastatic phenotype.
we identified a new mouse model of metastasis and a new mechanism of metastasis in this mouse model.

we have identified a novel molecular pathway in the progression of G0F p53 papilloma to carcinoma, which may lead in the future to the development of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of SCCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the progression of Gof p53 papilloma to SCC is associated with the amplification of MyC and Aurora Kinase A and that this progression is also marked by the acquisition epithelial-to-metastasis transition signatures.
the progression of Goff p53 tumors is associated with genomic instability, whereas the progression of LOF p53 is characterized by a higher rate of chromosomal instability.
the gain-of-function mutant p53R17H has a profound impact in skin carcinogenesis.
